purpose: Decide whether Skill-Pro can replace Skill-SP as the primary recent peer-reviewed carrier for STRI's representation-invariant evolution question, without promoting a released-code specialization into a paper-level universal claim.

required: persistent evolving artifact with explicit identity
identity participates in an observable learning/evolution seam
exact-refinement intervention can hold semantic content and evidence fixed
real downstream benchmark exists in the first-party method
source pin and replay seam can be frozen before model-level expansion
not_sufficient_alone: a source-code witness without downstream propagation

carrier.name: Skill-Pro
carrier.paper: Skill-Pro: Learning Reusable Skills from Experience via Non-Parametric PPO for LLM Agents
carrier.role_if_qualified: primary recent flagship lifecycle/evolution carrier; Skill-SP remains a deterministic mechanistic specialization rather than the paper root

source_pin.note: An initial git clone failed on the remote host due to TLS termination; a codeload archive was then fetched and independently pinned to the current main commit returned by git ls-remote. The commit-specific archive matches the earlier main snapshot on all load-bearing files.

qualified_control_seams.identity_schema: Skill.name is an explicit persistent field; Experience.skill stores skill-name attribution.
qualified_control_seams.identity_local_evidence: SkillEvolution stores Experience records in experience_buffer keyed by Skill name.
qualified_control_seams.released_readiness_specialization: SkillEvolution defaults to threshold=6 and marks a Skill ready only when len(experience_buffer[sk.name]) >= threshold.
qualified_control_seams.ordering: run.py executes Skill Evolution before SkillPool.maintain; native semantic deduplication therefore occurs after the readiness seam.
qualified_control_seams.native_semantic_dedup: SkillPool._semantic_dedup_inplace clusters semantic duplicates at cosine threshold 0.95 and keeps a representative, but the audited maintenance path does not pre-merge SkillEvolution evidence buffers.
qualified_control_seams.selection_surface: Skill identities are also enumerated/selected separately; this surface must be isolated from the lifecycle experiment rather than mixed into P0/P1.

independent_projection.key_result: At M=6, canonical 6 is ready; exact 3+3 has q=1 and p=0.5, so the semantic class is evidence-sufficient while no identity reaches the released readiness gate. Pre-gate reunion restores readiness; identity-only late dedup does not.

author_scheduler_probe.stub_boundary: only evolve and _compute_skill_logprobs were overridden, both after the author's identity distribution and readiness branch
author_scheduler_probe.key_result: Canonical and ID-placebo reach post-readiness hooks; exact 3+3 returns before either hook; pre-gate quotient reaches the hooks; identity-only reunion after the first local gate still does not.

operator_specialization.scope_warning: M=6 and q/p are a released-code specialization of the current pinned implementation. They are not asserted as a theorem about the Skill-Pro paper or self-evolving agents in general.

why_stronger_than_skill_sp_as_primary: peer-reviewed ICML 2026 Spotlight rather than an arXiv-only release
skill evolution is the paper's central scientific object rather than a peripheral controller detail
the first-party implementation exposes both persistent skill state and an identity-local evolution seam
the first-party method has real task environments suitable for downstream propagation tests
why_not_yet_sufficient_for_manuscript_re: P0 establishes scheduler reachability, not candidate quality or PPO-Gate outcome
no held-out task-performance consequence has yet been established
natural prevalence of exact-equivalence fragmentation has not been measured
cross-system replication on another recent flagship carrier is still required for a broad generality claim

next_required_evidence: P1: frozen real first-party trajectories, identical across attribution arms, through semantic-gradient candidate generation and PPO Gate
P2: preregistered held-out behavioral replay from the resulting frozen skill pools
cross-carrier: at least one additional 2026 flagship representation family or a representation-aware positive control
